summary: Derived two author candidates pending distinct review. Candidate1 gives the positive selected-prime expansion with repeated-square error, Cauchy into a nonnegative all-signed-cofactor square, explicit zero-cofactor support and coprime determinant equivalence, and uniform raw/comparison absolute and shared-prime bounds. The raw bounds use a reconstructed AP tau-square estimate rather than assigning integrality to shared determinant solutions. Candidate2 uses accepted corrected MOMENTS-010, checks its extension to x<=H<=x log^B x, fixes real eta and a psi plateau, constructs the conjugated endpoint function and primitive support, derives the no-H-loss sector/cell Gram pairing, proves a separate positive one-edge bad-state replacement, and reassembles ordered harmonic shared lists with all d0/D,V and factorial normalization. It yields the stated xY log^(-A) quadratic difference for the specified complete H-fold comparison, pending hostile review. No mn<H mask enters the operator, no unequal ambient normalizer identity is assumed, and Qmajor itself is not estimated. Actual-prime, major-energy, polynomial-rough/h=1/nonzero-center, full-source, novelty and Goldbach obligations remain. Usage is unknown.

claims.text: The selected-prime positive target admits the stated overlap error and signed nonnegative cofactor-square enlargement; determinant equivalence requires coprime a,b and the retained integer quotient conditions.
The reconstructed divisor-square progression estimate and full-pullback congruence give the stated absolute raw/comparison and shared-prime bounds uniformly in the H range.

For the specified eligible TypeII model, accepted moment scope plus the derived endpoint, positive bad-edge and ordered shared-list identities yield the stated Qall-Qmajor bound, pending separate review.
The assertion that a shared-a,b determinant equation alone enforces integer cofactors is refuted by the displayed finite witness.
Qmajor and actual-prime major-energy/decomposition/weight-removal estimates, polynomial-rough lower margins and prime boundary, novelty and Goldbach remain unestablished.
